black.tagline: Last to arrive. First to apologize. Never on time.
black.threatLevel: Fourth place. Allied, again. Bribing on time, finally, from a bag.
knownFor: Being the last team to submit a name (PNN-001).
Bribing the witches before the witches had opened for business (PNN-002).
Being webbed by the Pyro Posse, then announced last (PNN-005).
Getting caught in a giant pink web, exactly as PNN drew it in its first case (PNN-016).
Hitting four teams first, then being 'neutralised' in a rival's mission log (PNN-018).
An alleged alliance with the Area 51 Bureau, which both teams deny with matching enthusiasm (PNN-018).
Posting a stack of prank photos at 12:48 a.m. with no caption, before the homeowners saw them, then watching two witch waves bury the post (PNN-019).
A team name that is three words and a second B.
Reportedly splitting over toilet paper in the rain, then papering every house anyway (PNN-020).
Tying the Area 51 Bureau for Creepiest Team Prank, and tying a ring of macarons for Best Witch Bribe with Oreos in a black bag (PNN-021).
black.file:
The **Black Webb Bandits** chose spiders, a creature famous for patience, planning, and sitting very still until something happens to it. They then embodied the theme perfectly. The first entry in the file is the name reveal: last in the neighborhood, with a pun so tightly packed that PNN suspects it took a full week to find the second B.

The second entry is the bribe. Having failed to be first, the Bandits went for early. They arrived with treats and a flier asking 'Are you a witch?' before the witches had announced the instructions. The witches said NO. The Bandits are the only team in the game to have visited a starting line and somehow finished behind it.

The third entry is the Pyro Posse's visit, which wrapped a For Sale sign in orange cobweb and left a field of orange flags in the grass. The Bandits were pranked, and then, adding insult to webbing, announced last. A spider caught in someone else's web is a headline PNN has now written twice.

The fourth entry closes the loop. In **PNN-016**, shortly after midnight, the Prowling Purrpetrators strung **a giant pink web** across the Bandits' front walk, caught their spiders in it, and left a bottle of 'Black Web Spider Spray' at the scene. *No webs. No spiders. No problem.* PNN drew this exact scene in its very first case and called it a reconstruction. It is now a photograph. For once in this game, somebody showed up later than the Bandits.

The fifth entry is a partnership nobody will confirm. On the night of October 20, 2026 (**PNN-018**), the Bandits hit four teams, and then the Area 51 Bureau hit four teams, **including the Bandits' own house.** The two teams hit **the same Pyro Posse house and the same Tightie Whities house,** split the Silver Bullets down the middle, and skipped the pink house together. The Bureau's logs mention the Bandits eight times, call their toilet paper 'basic,' and report them 'neutralised.' The Bureau also strapped the Bandits' signature spider to a cow. For once, the Bandits were first at every shared house. It is also the most attention the Bandits have received since the name reveal. PNN calls this progress.

The sixth entry is the Bandits being early, which nobody had prepared for. On the night of October 21, 2026 (**PNN-019**), they wrapped bundles on the pink and red porches and posted the proof at **12:48 a.m.,** a stack of attachments and **zero words,** before either household was likely to see it. The post landed behind a big witch message from the day before, and another big one buried it today. *For once the Bandits were first, and for once it did not help.* The post was answering the pink web of PNN-016, **two days and nineteen minutes late.** PNN calls that a rapid response.

PNN has also heard, and cannot confirm, that the Bandits' ranks split over whether to toilet-paper their last round of pranks at all, since rain was on the way. *In the end, they papered every one.* **Spiders love rain. Toilet paper does not.** *A team that needed a week to pick a name needed an evening to argue with the sky, and the roll won (PNN-020).*

In fairness, the Bandits have charm, a genuinely great logo, and a name that makes people say 'oh, I get it.' Those are real assets. Clueso notes that none of them are punctuality, or web security.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *The Bandits finished fourth with 23 points.* **They tied for Best Witch Bribe with Oreos in a black bag,** *a bribe that matched the team colors and the store shelf.* **They were too early to bribe in PNN-002. This time they were on time, and tied with homemade macarons.** *PNN's pastry desk is still investigating.*

They also tied for **Creepiest Team Prank,** *with the Area 51 Bureau.* **The Black-and-Green Alliance (PNN-018) has now shared two houses, one cow, a creepy prank award, and a bribe vote.** *The Bandits insist the Bureau is a rival. The trophy case would be a duplex.*
strengths: A genuinely good name.
Excellent logo. Eight legs, no regrets.
A flair for dramatic entrances, when they arrive.
weaknesses: Starting lines, finish lines, and every line in between.
Partners who write four mission logs.
Group chats with witches in them.
black.advice: Set an alarm. Then a second alarm. Look up before you step outside. And next time, bake the bribe: the bag got a vote, but the macarons got a look.

green.tagline: The truth is out there. So is the trash. So are the cows.
green.threatLevel: Second place. Briefly a trespasser at a real restricted facility. Excellent caterer.
knownFor: Being outed by its own recycling (PNN-004).
Meeting the pink team in California, then pranking a pink house back home (PNN-009).
Declaring a 'cosmic lockdown' on the pink team, then hosting a rodeo four days later (PNN-013).
A team name that promises secrets and a trash can that kept none.
Hitting the same two houses as the Black Webb Bandits, then the Bandits themselves (PNN-018).
Four Mission Logs, four verdicts, and a cow with a wardrobe (PNN-018).
Agents, a saucer, and a cow with a complaint. Now several cows.

Solving a Tide clue at the New Haven Residential Treatment Center, getting a police threat from the staff, then going to a school instead of the party, then winning both food awards and second place (PNN-021).
Party treats so good that members of the pink team are eating the leftovers for breakfast (PNN-021).
green.file:
The **Area 51 Bureau** built its brand on secrecy: agents, a flying saucer, a cow in mid-abduction. A team like that is supposed to be impossible to catch. Then the Pyro Posse crowned two garbage cans with balloons and tissue-paper flames, and the Bureau's cover-up was blown by its own driveway.

PNN reminds the Bureau that Roswell was a long time ago and this was in front of the house. The cans were not abducted. They were accessorized. For a team that exists to bury the truth, there are now several balloons on it.

In PNN-009 the Bureau went on offense. It met the pink team at a theme park, learned when it was driving home, and landed a foil-hatted patio umbrella on a pink lawn. It then announced it had 'closed the case' on the pink team and put its pranking days on **'cosmic lockdown.'** It also called the pink team 'a little pale.'

The lockdown lasted four days. In **PNN-013**, the Bureau woke up to **two inflatable aliens in cowboy hats riding cows branded 'PP'** on its own lawn, with alien beef jerky at the door. A Bureau built to explain the unexplained could not explain its front yard. PNN rated the morning expression 'befuddled.'

The fourth entry is the one the Bureau would prefer to classify. On the night of October 20, 2026 (**PNN-018**), the Bureau hit four teams, **two of them the same houses as the Black Webb Bandits,** and then the Bandits' own house. It posted four Mission Logs, mentioned the Bandits eight times, and issued four verdicts, a function PNN reserves for itself. Its cow arrived at each stop dressed for the house: briefs, a mohawk, a flame brand. The Bureau calls the Bandits rivals. The Bureau's schedule says otherwise, and so does the Bureau's cow.

In fairness, the Bureau's own pranks are ambitious, well-traveled, and catered. Its only real vulnerabilities are the things it cannot classify: the curb, the calendar, and cattle.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *A scavenger hunt clue about Tide and getting clean sent six teams to the Tide Cleaners store.* **The Bureau went to the New Haven Residential Treatment Center.** *It got out, it snooped, and the administrators threatened to call the police if it did not leave immediately.* **After twenty cases of pretending to be a secret facility, the Bureau finally met a real one, and got the authentic restricted-area experience.** *The Bureau's own witch sat in silence, keeping her promise not to help, apparently prepared to let the police handle it first.*

At the last clue, the Bureau tied the pink team, then misread the final instructions and went to a nearby school. **It arrived at the party late and fed it anyway:** *Best Party Food, Best Party Dessert, a share of the bribe vote for frosted Nutter Butters, and a share of Creepiest Team Prank with the Bandits.* **25 points, second place.** *The treats were so good that members of the pink team are still eating the leftovers for breakfast.* **Out of this world, as advertised.** *It just took the scenic route through two zoning categories.*
strengths: A genuinely good logo, with agents.
Total commitment to the bit. The bit is secrecy.
A flying saucer on call. It is an umbrella, but it is on call.
Four mission logs in one night, with emojis.
weaknesses: Anything visible from space, including balloons.
green.advice: Bring the bins in. Count your cows. And when a clue says "clean," try the dry cleaner first.

orange.threatLevel: Third place. First to finish. Briefly scattered.
knownFor: A fire theme delivered, in PNN-004, with balloons.
Three pranks in one night, plus a fourth they forgot to mention (PNN-005).
Telling the game group 'It's like we're the only ones playing.'
Calling the PNN newsletter spam, then replying with canned meat (PNN-006).
A screaming glitter bomb and a plan spelled 'stratogy' (PNN-008).
Being hit by three teams in two nights: the pink team, then the Bandits and the Bureau, together (PNN-017, PNN-018).
Being purr-manently extinguished in a kiddie pool, then thanking the pink team for the Spam (PNN-017).
Replying to the Whities' last-minute sweep with a relationship status, 'lucky underwear,' and four emojis (PNN-020).
Posse on fire 🔥 at the scavenger hunt: first to finish, two points, and a witch on the roster who reportedly guided by hmm (PNN-021).
Finally dressing like a fire team: the party agreed the costumes looked like a cartoon fire warrior in his final form, flame hair and gold chain included (PNN-021).
orange.file:
The **Pyro Posse** arrived with the boldest brand in the game: fire, a promise to 'bring them to ash,' and poster art that looks like it has its own budget. Then they went to the party store. In PNN-004 the flames were balloons and tissue paper. PNN admires the confidence. PNN also admires the receipt.

By PNN-005 the Posse had escalated to actual laundry, actual smoke, and a poem narrated by underwear. They pranked the Tightie Whities, the Silver Bullets, and the Black Webb Bandits in a single night. That is a lot of work. It is also a lot of photos, which the Posse posted to the game group before the victims got home, spoiling the surprise for exactly the people it was built for.

> Sometimes I am fast…. Usually when I shouldn’t be.
> — a Pyro Posse member, on the deleted photos

The Posse also declared, 'It’s like we’re the only ones playing,' which is what a runner says after the first mile of a marathon. Then it called PNN's newsletter spam (PNN-006), mailed the pink team a screaming glitter bomb with a typo in the strategy (PNN-008), and announced its pranking had 'concluded.'

It had not concluded. It had been **scheduled.** In **PNN-017**, the last stop of the pink team's six-house night, the Posse's lawn received **a kiddie pool of crying pumpkins, a can of Spam stamped with a paw print, and a sign declaring it 'Purr-manently Extinguished.'** The next morning, the Posse thanked the pink team for replacing the Spam it had eaten for dinner. *The team that called a newsletter spam had Spam for dinner.* PNN has framed the sentence.

In **PNN-020,** the Tightie Whities hit all six teams two hours before the deadline, and the Posse answered first: *'we were on you from the start! We found your missing lucky underwear at our house.'* **The Posse was on them from the start: PNN-005, a clothesline.** It then lectured the Whities on waiting until the last minute. *The team that posted its prank and deleted it before the victims got home has opinions on timing.*

For the record, PNN reminds the Posse that actual fire is not part of the game. A paper flame on a stick delivers all the drama and none of the paperwork. The Posse owns a great many paper flames. It now also owns a pool.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *Posse on fire 🔥 at the scavenger hunt.* **After twenty cases of balloons, laundry, and Spam, the Posse finally dressed like a fire team:** *the party agreed the costumes looked like a cartoon fire warrior in his final form, with spiky flame-red hair, sun tattoos, and a gold chain.* **The flames were decorative. The commitment was not.** **The Posse finished first, for two points.** *The Posse also had a witch on its roster, who promised not to help and, by every account, did not give directions.* **Witnesses say she did not need to.** *When the clue talk drifted, she reportedly offered a thoughtful "huh, I wouldn't have thought of it like that," and a great many hmms.* **PNN calls it a game of hot and cold, the fire team's native language.**

The Posse reached the party first, on foot in the driveway, just as the pink team came up it, horn first. **The Posse scattered like startled pumpkins, unharmed and briefly relocated.** *The team that once rang that pink door with a screaming glitter bomb (PNN-008) now knows how a scream at that door sounds from the other side.* **Final: third, 24 points.**
strengths: Effort. Real, enormous, visible effort.
Poster art that could frighten a lesser team.
Gracious in defeat, at least about canned meat.
weaknesses: The delete button, which they find too late.
orange.advice: Wait until the victim has seen the prank before you post it. Learn to read a hmm. And when you hear a horn in a pink driveway, you already know what to do.

pink.threatLevel: Champions. Everywhere at once. Uncatchable, until the witches handed them trophies.
knownFor: Being the team Inspector Clueso is certain is guilty.
The Pink Sweep: six teams pranked in one night, in order, with zero arrests (PNN-012 to PNN-017).
Signing every scene with a panther, a paw print, and a monogram.
Catching an entire pirate crew with one teen and one foam dart (PNN-010).
Running a whole newsroom, hotline, newsletter, and Corrections Desk.
Winning the PNN-006 exchange in three sentences and a hyperlink.
Being the one house neither the Black Webb Bandits nor the Area 51 Bureau would touch (PNN-018).
Being 'caught' by a sticker and a poster on its own porch and remaining uncaught (PNN-019).
Guilty until proven guilty.
Being hit by the Tightie Whities last-minute and still uncaught, and a re-lettered 'Not Tonight' that PNN counts as a compliment (PNN-020).
Accidentally throwing six gender reveals: neighbors reportedly congratulated pranked houses on a baby girl (PNN-020).
Winning the 2026 Broomstick Challenge with 28 points, and sweeping Most Creative Team Name, Best Costumes, Funniest Team Prank, and Most Visible Team Prank (PNN-021).
pink.file:
The **Prowling Purrpetrators** spent most of the season as the only team Inspector Clueso could not put in a case file. The file was very thick. It contained nothing. Clueso said the thickness was the point.

Other teams came to the pink team instead, and each left with less than it brought. The Pyro Posse's glitter bomb was defused and its cookies eaten (PNN-008). The Area 51 Bureau's raid arrived with cookies too (PNN-009). The Crimson Crew was caught by one teen with a foam dart and begged to finish (PNN-010).

Then came **October 19.** Between about 11 p.m. and 1 a.m., the pink team pranked **every other team in the game:** underwear for the Tightie Whities, branded cattle for the Area 51 Bureau, a flag and a treasure chest for the Crimson Crew, a retirement party for the Silver Bullets, a web for the Black Webb Bandits, and a kiddie pool for the Pyro Posse. *(PNN-012 to PNN-017.)* Every scene was signed. Four group portraits were posed at the scene. The Crimson Crew reviewed its own prank as 'top-tier entertainment.'

Clueso finally had evidence. **He has arrested no one.** PNN's own privacy desk blurred the faces, the Crimson Crew kept the footage, the Silver Bullets slept through it, and the aliens only smiled. He has filed a grievance against his own newsroom. It is in its second binder.

In **PNN-019,** the Black Webb Bandits finally answered the web of PNN-016, **two days and nineteen minutes late.** They wrapped a bundle on the pink porch, put a pink panther sticker on it, and posted a poster of a panther upside down in a cocoon. **The panther looks calm, half-lidded, and mildly inconvenienced.** Clueso, who has spent eighteen cases trying to catch the pink team, reports that the Bandits caught a sticker. **The pink team remains caught nowhere.** *It wears a cocoon better than the Bandits wear a deadline.*

In **PNN-020,** the Tightie Whities hit the pink house with the other five, two hours before the deadline, with a satin pair that looks a lot like the 'Not Tonight' of PNN-012. *The pink team's props are now good enough to be reused.* **No pink suspects were caught.** PNN has also heard, and cannot confirm, that some houses the pink team pranked were later approached by neighbors with congratulations on a baby girl, apparently mistaking the pink lights and pink toilet paper for a gender reveal. *PNN has no word of any baby. It has every word of pink.* **Clueso regards this as the most convincing alibi to date.**

The Purrpetrators decline to comment. They are, as always, wearing sunglasses.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *On October 24, 2026, the Prowling Purrpetrators hosted the party, at the same pink house where the game began, and then won it.* **28 points: first place, three ahead of the field.** *They tied the Area 51 Bureau to the last clue, drove the straightest line to the finish while the Bureau went to a school, and arrived in their own driveway with the horn on.* **Their witch bribe was homemade paw-shaped sugar cookies ringed with French macarons.** *It tied a bag of Oreos. PNN's pastry desk has not recovered.*

Some guests asked how a team could host and win. **An unbiased third party, the witches and every voter at the party, found no foul play.** *Just competitive play and investigative prowess.* **Pink, the least Halloween color on the wheel, won the Halloween game.** *Nobody looks for pink in October. That was the plan.*
strengths: An extremely good logo.
Route planning: six houses, one night, no wrong turns.
A newsroom, a hotline, and a newsletter, all on one team.
Sunglasses.
Composure, even in a cocoon.
Decor so convincing the neighbors congratulated people (rumored).
weaknesses: Winning arguments before the other team finishes typing, which Clueso is treating as a lack of sportsmanship.
Posing for group photos at the scene, which Clueso would call a weakness if any of the faces were visible.
Cocoons, which Clueso says should have worked.
pink.advice: Clueso asked you to prank someone. You pranked everyone. Then you won. He would like to rephrase every request he has ever made.

red.tagline: Caught on the way in. Boarded on the way out.
red.threatLevel: Tied for fifth. Boarded by a Knight in double overtime. Deserted by its own rat. Spared by the witches.
knownFor: Being caught red-handed by one teen with a foam blaster (PNN-010).
A plea of candy that was last Halloween's.
Free Halloween decorating for the pink house, installed under supervision.
Watching the pink team board its porch on camera, holding its fire, and calling it 'top-tier entertainment' (PNN-014).
Dropping a purr and a B from other teams' names in one evening.
Having a pirate shrink-wrapped on its own porch while the lookout watched for pink (PNN-019).
Reviewing the Whities' last-minute sweep as 'top tier entertainment' again and calling the briefs 'emergency sails' (PNN-020).
Arriving last to the hunt meetup after No. 2 BYU fell to UCF in double overtime, and sailing the hunt with morale below deck (PNN-021).
Returning from the hunt one ingredient short: a white rat, later seen on the Patriot Park fields. The witches waived the one-point penalty on an eyewitness account (PNN-021).
red.file:
**The Crimson Crew** spent weeks as the only team without a case file. Clueso circled its name in red pen. The Crew answered by sailing to six houses in one night and getting caught at one. *(PNN-010.)*

The catch was brief. **One teen, one foam dart, several grown pirates, and a great deal of begging.** The Crew paid in candy that was last Halloween's. The taste panel declined to reopen the account. The Crew also hung skull bunting at the pink house and left a laminated poster announcing 'Your ship is ours!', which PNN counts as free decorating and has thanked.

Two nights later the pink team returned the visit. In **PNN-014**, a boarding party hoisted **a pink flag on the Crew's own flagpole** and left **a treasure chest marked 'PP'** on the doormat. The Crew's 'security glass' watched the whole thing. The Crew **held its fire,** later explaining it had assumed all the pink was for a cause, and reviewed the evening as **'top-tier entertainment.'** PNN has never had a victim publish a five-star review. The ship is, as the Crew once put it, ours.

In **PNN-019,** the Black Webb Bandits visited the Crew's steps on the night of October 21, 2026. They left **a bundle with a Jolly Roger sticker on top,** plastic spiders across the 'Home Sweet Home' mat, and toilet paper in the trees. *The lookout that spotted pink boarders at a hundred yards in PNN-014 missed an entire spider operation.* **PNN calls this the Clueso condition: color-selective vision.** The proof was posted at 12:48 a.m., before the Crew could comment.

In **PNN-020,** the Tightie Whities hit the Crew with two hours left on the deadline. The Crew's review: *'another spectacular top tier entertainment value observed from our looking glass,'* and **the briefs are 'the emergency sails for when we cruise to an easy victory.'** PNN notes the Crew has now reviewed pranks on itself as top tier twice, and has caught none of them. *The looking glass is a fine instrument. It does not have a door.*

In fairness, any team that reaches six houses in one night has range, and any team that reviews its own pranking that generously has class. The Crew's range simply ends at the color pink.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *The hunt was delayed until the BYU game ended, and No. 2 BYU lost to UCF in double overtime.* **The Crew was the last team to fully arrive, and PNN believes the most invested in the result.** *A pirate expects to be boarded by pink (PNN-014). He does not expect to be boarded by a Knight, in Orlando, on a penalty.* **Morale: below deck. Compass: still pointed at Orlando.** *Final: tied for fifth, 22 points.*

*In fairness, the Crew showed up heartbroken and played the whole game anyway, and any team that can finish a scavenger hunt in mourning has a pirate's spirit.* **It simply sails better when nobody is checking the score.**

**The cleanup.** *The Crew came back one ingredient short: a white rat from Patriot Park.* **Another team reported seeing a white rat on the Patriot Park fields.** *Rats desert a sinking ship, and the Crew's ship had gone down in double overtime that afternoon.* **A missing ingredient normally costs a point. The witches took the eyewitness account and waived it.** *The Crew lost the game, the ship, and the rat, and kept every point. PNN calls it the luckiest bad day in the file.*
strengths: Range: six houses in one night.
Props that commit to the bit.
Sportsmanship: the only victim to leave a five-star review.
red.advice: Check the lights before the lawn. Pay the teen. Widen the lookout's color settings. And next season, mute the game until the hunt is over.

silver.tagline: Dinner at four. Six homes by 7:30. Bed by eight. Party at midnight, unattended.
silver.threatLevel: Tied for fifth. Werewolves, allegedly. Possibly checked in at a retirement center. In bed, definitely.
knownFor: Pranking six families by 7:30 p.m., then going to bed (PNN-011).
Sleeping through its own midnight retirement party (PNN-015).
A 'Warewolf Management Division' with a hotline that does not exist.
A clothesline of unidentified laundry hung at their home during the football game (PNN-005).
Being split between the Bandits and the Bureau, one Silver house each, like a pie (PNN-018).
A poster calling them 'Slow, Unsure, and Completely Disoriented.'
Insisting the team name is about werewolves, then leaving the party first, past bedtime (PNN-021).
Calling in a missing clue at the retirement center that the witches later found exactly where it was left. PNN suspects the staff escorted the team inside (PNN-021).
silver.file:
The **Silver Bullets** chose a name meant to be fast, shiny, and fatal to monsters. For weeks PNN saw none of the three. Then, on **October 19**, the team ate dinner at four, pranked **six families** by 7:30, and was reportedly home and in bed before eight. *(PNN-011.)*

The plan was sound. With the last week of pranking underway, the Bullets took first pick of un-pranked porches while the rest of the neighborhood was still doing the dishes. One household watched the entire evening and reviewed it in writing: *'evidence, bullets, fur and so much flannel.'* The review ended with a bedtime.

The Bullets' announcement closed with a hotline for the 'SB Warewolf Management Division.' PNN checked. **No such hotline exists.** PNN's does: **+1 (801) 79-PRANK.** The Division is welcome to it.

The same night, a little after midnight, the pink team threw the Bullets **a retirement party** *(PNN-015)*: a Happy Retirement banner, a balloon arch, pink cupcakes, senior coupons, and **a skeleton in a 'RETIRED' tiara** as guest of honor. By every indication, the guests of honor slept through it. The Division's hotline, which does not exist, received no calls. By sunrise the driveway was pink enough to be seen from the early-bird buffet.

In fairness, a team that tells you when it will be home and then is home is the most reliable team in the game. The Bullets were slow in PNN-005, and they are fast now. They are simply not awake at midnight, which, under Rule 7, is exactly how the game is supposed to work.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *The Bullets spent the party explaining that their name is about werewolves, not about being elderly.* **PNN's folklore desk notes that silver bullets are what you use on a werewolf, which makes the team the werewolf's problem, not the werewolf.** *They were also the first team to leave, well past their bedtime.* **A werewolf that leaves before the moon is fully up is a wolf with an alarm clock.**

*During the hunt, the Bullets called in to report their clue missing from the retirement center.* **When the witches went to clean up, they found it there, exactly where it was supposed to be.** *PNN's theory: the staff saw the Silver Bullets wandering the grounds after dark, assumed some residents had slipped out, and kindly escorted them back inside.* **PNN cannot confirm the escort, the blanket, or the pudding. PNN can confirm the clue never moved.**

*In fairness, they finished the whole game, tied for fifth with 22 points, and were home on schedule, which is the most reliable thing anyone did all night.*
strengths: Timing. Fast, early, and punctual to a fault.
Costumes with commitment: flannel, fur, silver, and a moon in shorts.
A bedtime that has never once been missed, not even for a party in their honor.
weaknesses: Witnesses with a good view and a way with words.
Hotlines that exist only on paper.
Late nights, in all forms, including their own retirement.
silver.advice: Save the hotline number. It is +1 (801) 79-PRANK. Dial before bedtime. And if you are going to be werewolves, stay up for the moon at least once.

white.tagline: Tight name. Loose story. Fast cleanup.
white.threatLevel: Tied for fifth. Dressed in their own evidence. Cape last seen in a car.
knownFor: Two dogs, two walks, and a very awkward 'how long have you had it?' (PNN-003).
Being the target of the most obvious prank in the history of obvious pranks (PNN-005).
Carrying plates of treats to doors that never opened, on 'the wrong night' (PNN-007).
Getting out-underweared at its own theme: monogrammed briefs and a 'Not Tonight' sign (PNN-012).
Being hit by three teams in two nights, with a cow in monogrammed briefs as the finale (PNN-012, PNN-018).
The fastest cleanup in the game.
Hitting all six other teams with two hours left on the deadline, then announcing it was 'back in the game' (PNN-020).
Spelling its own name two ways in one night: 'Tighty' in the message, 'Tightie' on the notice (PNN-020).
Dressing as Captain Underpants in underwear recycled from pranks pulled on them, then entering a Boot Barn without the cape (PNN-021).
white.file:
The **Tightie Whities** named their team after underwear and then, remarkably, acted surprised. Anyone who names a team that way has pre-approved the joke. The Pyro Posse took the invitation literally and hung a clothesline of laundry on their walk. Then they lit it.

The garment in question was a pair of white satin bloomers. They are not tight. After treatment, they are not white. The charring ran down the middle in a pattern a banner on the same line called 'The Skidmark Synod.' PNN did not name it. PNN would have fought for the word 'Synod' to be somewhere else.

Earlier, in PNN-003, the Whities were spotted walking dogs downhill a few minutes apart. When a neighbor asked how long one member had owned a dog, the answer was a pause. PNN has not recovered from the pause. Clueso filed it as *Operation Loose End* and has refused to elaborate. Then, in PNN-007, the team carried plates of treats from door to door, found no one home, and concluded: *'Man, we picked the wrong night.'*

The pink team supplied the right one. In **PNN-012**, the first stop of the pink team's six-house night, the Whities' trees were papered with paw-stamped toilet paper, a clothesline of **briefs monogrammed 'PP'** crossed the yard, and **giant pink satin underwear** on the porch read **'Not Tonight. You Know Why...'** The homeowners drove in mid-prank and could barely park. By morning, the yard was spotless. *They were hit briefly. The cleanup was briefer.*

In **PNN-020,** with two hours left on the deadline, the Whities, who had barely played all season, finally did the pranking: **all six other teams in one night,** *the same count as the Pink Sweep.* Their warning ran 'The Tighty Whities are back in the game. Watch out for last-minute pranking.' **The notice on the porch spelled it 'Tightie.'** The evidence: a lantern in briefs, a pink satin pair that looks a lot like the 'Not Tonight' of PNN-012 with new fine print, white plastic over a lawn, and a door dressed as underwear with a sign about a 'Solid #2.' *The Pyro Posse found 'lucky underwear' and the Crimson Crew found 'emergency sails.'* PNN calls it the right night at the wrong hour. It is the closest the Whities have come to the right answer.

The team has a tight name, a loose story, and a gift for being the one everyone notices. In fairness, that is the right gift for a team named after underwear: you cannot go unnoticed. You can only be uncovered, and then, very quickly, cleaned up.

**The final night (PNN-021).** *The Whities came to the hunt as Captain Underpants: underwear over their pants, red capes, and briefs repurposed from pranks pulled on them.* **The first team in PNN history to wear its own case file.** *Then a clue led into the Boot Barn, and one Whitie ran in without her cape.* **The employees did not see a superhero. They saw only the underpants.** *The cape stayed in the car, heroically doing nothing.*

The team confessed that its name backfired: **it planned to be the team doing the underwear, and everyone did the underwear to it.** *That is what happens when you prank last (PNN-020).* **Final: tied for fifth, 22 points, every one of them earned.**
strengths: Absolute commitment to the premise.
A name that sells itself.
The fastest cleanup crew in the neighborhood.
weaknesses: The word 'loose,' which has followed them everywhere.
A printer that disagrees with the team spokesperson.
white.advice: Rehearse saying "about two years." Lock the clothesline. Check the calendar before you carry a plate. And always, always bring the cape inside.
